quest.title: A Knight's Pursuit
quest.description: What price must one pay in pursuit of power that surpasses mortal ken...?
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x425, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: *sigh* It pains me to say it, but my sword-swinging days are over. If I went with you, I'd only get in the way.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Guess I'll be handling today's routine work all by my lonesome.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Grandpa Adorno!

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Oh, little Paimon, and the Honorary Knight!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Feeling better today?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Right as rain! I wasn't really injured yesterday. Theodore had a look at me, and frankly, I'm feeling better than ever!

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: I've his treatment to thank for my continued vigor. Without his help, they'd probably have buried me years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Theodore... You mean the apprentice medic from the 8th Company? He didn't look all that skilled to Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: He once aspired to be a knight fighting on the front lines, but perhaps the physician's path suits him better.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Anyway, enough about that for now. Did you guys come here looking for Lohen?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, he disappeared after trying the Simulation Training Bubble yesterday. We can't find him anywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did he come back here?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Yeah, he left a note this morning... Said he wanted to apologize for what happened yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: He confessed that yesterday was all just an act, and that he couldn't stand this bone-dry daily routine, so, to make up for it...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: "...I'll wipe out every last one of those annoying monsters."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's how he apologizes? Heh. Totally his style.

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: Hmm... Ordinary monsters pose no threat to him. What worries me is that something like what happened yesterday might happen again...

response.speaker: Adorno
response.text: If you could keep an eye on him, that would certainly put me at ease.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Mmhmm, I'll keep an eye out.

choices.text: Should we go check on him?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A short while earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Guess you're the last one... You'd better put up a good fight!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Hmm? Who's there!

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Ugh... It ran away...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: —I never thought a winery owner would care so much about hunting monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Or could it be you're after something else?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: And what about you? Are monsters all you aim to eradicate?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Given how the previous scene was so clean that "nothing" was left behind...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh? First I've heard of it.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: In that case, why don't we examine the monsters here? Perhaps we'll discover what it is about them that's attracting so much attention.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...Ah, forget it. I'll go after the one that got away. Investigations and the like aren't really my style.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: See you around... Diluc.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...That's the gist of everything that happened before you arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's he tryin' to pull, seriously... Forget "Punching Bag Knight," he should be the "Needs-A-Punch Knight"!

choices.text: So, what's the deal with these monsters?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Adorno talked about 'em yesterday... Sounded like they're kinda weird, but they haven't hurt anyone yet?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Which is partly down to someone secretly eliminating them... and partly down to them preferring to attack their own kind whenever hunger strikes.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They attack... their own kind?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Yes. Eyewitness reports are scarce, so we can't be certain, but the monster remains here do show signs that they've been fighting each other.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Forming packs, yet killing each other... It's not the behavior of naturally occurring monsters.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's certainly strange...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But if these monsters will attack each other, can't we just wait for them to wipe themselves out? Why be so vigilant?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Because such beasts, bearing Ursa's Flesh, have appeared before, and not just once, either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Varka!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Well, this is a coincidence. Honorary Knight, Paimon, and you too, Diluc.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: ...So, the Knights of Favonius are not entirely ignorant of this anomaly.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Yes... The tragedy Eroch wrought cannot — and will not — be allowed to happen again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you just say... Ursa's Flesh? Is this somehow related to that Eroch guy?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: In his pursuit of transcendent power, he once conspired with one of Dottore's Segments to extract a serum containing the power of Ursa the Drake from the dragon's flesh.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: When the reckoning with the Knights came, he and his cohorts all injected themselves with that serum... causing us quite a bit of trouble.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Their strength and bloodthirst increased in equal measure, and consumed by madness, they even attacked each other.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Ironically, Eroch ultimately failed to control that power. Not only did he turn his sword against his followers, but he went to his own demise in the process.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ursa the Drake... What exactly is it? How could it have such terrifying power?

choices.text: I heard it's existed for over a thousand years...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That's right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then... then why did they only seal it away? Was even the founding Grand Master unable to kill it?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: No. It was spared because... Ursa the Drake was once an angel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm sorry!?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I've heard that long ago, the angelic race was faced with a difficult choice... and Ursa chose to preserve its "power."

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Having lost its mind and retaining only power, this angel remained drawn to human settlements, not realizing that its proximity alone would destroy many...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Is that why Vennessa decided to seal it away back then?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Yes, but it was awakened by The Doctor's inducement... which was an oversight on the Knights' part. I won't deny that.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Rather than assigning blame for the past, we would be better served by rooting out the present threat.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: But Ursa's flesh and blood... Why would it reappear within these monsters?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Eroch was, admittedly, once a knight in whom we placed much of our hopes. As such, he knows our methods well.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Before he met his end, he destroyed all records regarding his experiment site.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: To this day, we've yet to find any information to locate it. I suspect we have the Segment to thank for that, too.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: #But Dottore's backup plans were dismantled by {NICKNAME} in Sumeru, a fact you're no doubt aware of.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: We believe this means that the covert measures he took in Mondstadt have also ceased to work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh... So those monsters... They all escaped from the experiment site!?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: I'm afraid it goes deeper than that — someone has likely restarted the experiments.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Past experiments... Ursa's flesh and blood... Angelic power...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Does this mean... that the power I sensed in Lohen yesterday is...)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: You noticed it too, then? During the commotion yesterday.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes. At the time, I...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: So it's possible that Lohen has been dabbling in forbidden experiments to gain extraordinary power?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He... He isn't bad enough to do something like that, is he?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Wealth, power, authority... Too many things can turn a good person into a villain.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Ursa, Eroch... Neither of them were the "bad guys" you might imagine before they made their fateful choices.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: But no matter Lohen's intentions, it is my duty to pull him back from the edge before he goes too far.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... What do we do now? Keep investigating in secret?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: No need for that. That's why I'm here at Dornman Port — I'm going to find him and ask him directly!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Slippery little rat. Pretty good at running away, aren't you?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Now... where will you go from here?

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Hey— Lohen!

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Now's not the time to be cleaning up test subjects! The Knights are making their move!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...Ugh.

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Lots of unfamiliar knights showed up in Dornman Port today... Did yesterday's test expose us? Or did they capture an experiment subject? Could they have discovered...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: It was only a matter of time. I'd say we were lucky to have lasted this long.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Heh... Steadfast allies make redoubtable opponents, as they say.

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: What do we do now, then? Find a place to lie low?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...That would make reaching our objective even harder.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: That you were able to come here freely means the Knights haven't verified their suspicions just yet. We have to go all-in while we still have the chance.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Do it now. Use me as a test subject.

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Now? But those problems we were having before... We still haven't...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Why are you hesitating? I told you, we're not the same, you and I. I'm doing this for myself.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Extraordinary power comes with extraordinary risks. I figured that out a long time ago.

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Do it. Now! Or have you forgotten your goal?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: *cough*

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: No! It's not working! ...Was the dosage too low? Or was the concentration too weak?

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Or maybe... the perfect result was never attainable...

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Lohen! We've got to hide! We can gather more monsters for experiments later...

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...No. No!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Hide? How much time do you think the Knights will give us, huh? We've always been gambling with a small window of opportunity.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Now we'd only confirm their suspicions if we ran. That would make us targets no matter where we resurface. How would we get close to our target then?

response.speaker: Theodore
response.text: Then... what should we do now?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: ...We're going to break the target out tonight.

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Then... he can follow us down to "Hell."

choices.text: And it even fought with the first Grand Master?
Are they worth all this fuss?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: As expected, the Knights of Favonius are acting swiftly...

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: There's a crowd gathering up ahead... Something about this feels wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: That's... Adorno!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A few hours ago...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Hah... I finally found you!

dialogues.speaker: Northland Cat
dialogues.text: Meow...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Keep a close eye on it now. Don't let it stray too far from you again, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Moricztill
dialogues.text: Thank you... Thank you, Grandpa Adorno!

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: And don't run off into the countryside alone looking for it again. I know you're worried about it, but Hannelore's worried about you, too. We'll keep this our secret this time, but don't let it happen again.

dialogues.speaker: Moricztill
dialogues.text: Okay... I understand.

dialogues.speaker: Northland Cat
dialogues.text: Meow...!

dialogues.speaker: Experimental Monster
dialogues.text: *roar*

dialogues.speaker: Moricztill
dialogues.text: Ah! A... A monster?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: A monster? How did it get here... Something about this one doesn't look right...

dialogues.speaker: Moricztill
dialogues.text: A—Ah... Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Don't be afraid! I'm here with you! Now stand up and get out of here!

dialogues.speaker: Moricztill
dialogues.text: B—But...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Run back home! Don't you worry — Gramps here... is a knight!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...The knights who arrived later defeated the monster... Its power far exceeded what is normal.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Adorno fought it tooth and nail to buy time until they arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Adorno... Adorno!

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Hah...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: ...It's fine. You know my condition... I wouldn't have made it this far without your help.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Fighting one last time to save others sure makes me feel more like a knight than lying in bed ever did! ... *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: I'm sorry to do this to you now... I know you worked hard on those treatments...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: Lohen... The title of "Benevolent Knight," and the 5th Company's captaincy...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: —If you don't want them, just let them go. Be true to yourself, that's all that matters.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Lohen, come with me for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The Investigative Team's analysis shows that the monster that attacked Adorno bears Ursa's mark.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Do you still intend to remain silent now that things have got this far?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: This isn't an interrogation. You can remain silent if you wish, but I hope you'll choose to come clean.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: —I'll talk.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...I'll confess everything and accept whatever punishment awaits. But, please...

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Please give me one more night. Tomorrow, I'll go to the Knights of Favonius and explain everything.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: ...I swear it on my honor as a knight.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...That's the first time I've heard you swear such an oath in all this time we've worked together.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: I know it doesn't carry much weight.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Then let's use the Benevolent Knight's name to balance the scales.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Please keep your promise this time, Lohen.

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry, Theodore...

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: I'd intended to make Lohen captain and leave my title to you... I know how much you've yearned for that title since you were little...

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: It's not your fault, Mr. Adorno...

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: I don't possess the talent that helped Lohen pass the Knights' exams so easily...

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: Years of work, and I'm still stuck as a trainee medic... How could I ever inherit your title?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: *cough*... Medics... Knights... We're all protecting people, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Adorno
dialogues.text: The way I see it, you earn that title every day...

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: ...No. In truth, I've done so much wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Theodore
dialogues.text: And what I'm about to do... is worse still...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...So you agreed to his request. Just like that?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: What else should I have done? Ask him to submit a report for my approval? Please. Spare us both.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I know how much Adorno means to him, so I trust the weight of his vow.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: There once was a man who made many promises to my father in the name of chivalry, yet in the end, he betrayed their friendship.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: "Warped obsessions and the passage of time can turn friends into foes as easily as the wind changes its course."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: ...Quoting Crepus, are we? That really takes me back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you guys... all know each other back in the day?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Once, there were three spirited young men who imagined their futures together.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: One was a rich young {RUBY#[D]Crepus}master. He dreamed of becoming a knight, but ended up inheriting the family winery.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Next came the hot-headed rule-b{RUBY#[S]Varka}reaker, who ended up leading the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: And the last {RUBY#[S]Eroch}one... obtained neither the wealth he desired, nor the power he yearned for.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Obsession was all that was left, piling up day after day into a towering spire.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that how Eroch... let The Doctor worm his way in?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Eroch made his own choices, no matter what was said to him.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I understand his reasoning, but that doesn't mean I pity him. And it certainly doesn't mean I'll make the same mistakes again.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I'm keeping a close eye on my subordinates this time...

response.speaker: Lietzberg
response.text: B—Bad news!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: —Hey, I haven't finished talking yet!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That voice... Did it come from where Adorno was just now?

choices.text: We can talk about trust later...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Lietzberg... What's going on here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Adorno's... gone? Lohen and Theodore, too?

response.speaker: Lietzberg
response.text: I don't know. I was on patrol, and I saw the door was wide open. I looked inside... and everything was like this!

response.speaker: Lietzberg
response.text: Captain Adorno couldn't have gotten out of bed in his condition. Could... someone have taken him away?

response.speaker: Wernher
response.text: Grand Master — it's an emergency! Vice Captain Lohen barreled straight through our patrols and headed for the outskirts!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: That kid... Seriously...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Did he leave any sort of message?

response.speaker: Wernher
response.text: Message? ... He looked like he was in a hurry. All he said was "Out of the way!" before rushing off.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did you go after him?

response.speaker: Wernher
response.text: Of course! But you know how fast he is. I'm afraid we...

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Track him as far as you can. Leave the rest to us!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Diluc, Honorary Knight, I'm counting on you to help me with this one.

choices.text: Let's hurry over and take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That Lohen! He just upped and left yesterday without saying a word...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's check in with Adorno and see if he's there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So many monsters... Huh? Wait, isn't that... Diluc?
